summary.text: The pure maiden whom Ovid names daughter of King Latinus and bride of Aeneas — the marriage for which Turnus fought and Latium went to war, in the Italian strand attested through Ovid's Metamorphoses rather than Virgil's Aeneid.

story.text: Ovid makes Lavinia the prize of the Laurentine settlement. Aeneas won the daughter of Latinus, Faunus' son, not without war; Turnus, indignant at losing a promised bride, rallied a fierce people until both sides forgot dower and father-in-law's scepter and fought only to conquer. When Turnus fell and Ardea burned, the Trojan captain took Lavinia and the Latin kingdom — the westward kingship Homer had foretold among the sons' sons of Dardanus.
